article_title: Generative artificial intelligence in secondary STEM education in the light of Human Flourishing: a scoping literature review
citation: Alissa Fock and Hans-Stefan Siller. (2025). Generative artificial intelligence in secondary STEM education in the light of Human Flourishing: a scoping literature review. International Journal of STEM Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40594-025-00589-5
title: Three OECD themes framing AI and Human Flourishing: broadening human capabilities, restoring meaning to individual lives, and developing new models for the future
description: The review adopts the OECD (2024b) framework of three themes for examining how AI shapes Human Flourishing: "AI and broadening human capabilities", "AI and restoring meaning to individual lives", and "AI and developing new models for the future". These themes structure both the theoretical specification of STEM Education for Human Flourishing and the three research questions of the review, and are used to evaluate to what extent current literature addresses the resulting research desiderata.
requirements: Applied to education considering both students and teachers as central players in educational processes
constraints: The authors state the elaborations are not exhaustive and serve as a preliminary specification for the field
target_learners: secondary school students in STEM disciplines
target_learning_goals: non-cognitive capabilities such as ethical decision-making, empathy, and perspective-taking alongside STEM disciplinary learning
examples: The review operationalizes the themes as three research questions on non-cognitive aspects and ethics, application and perception of generative AI, and development of new models
key_sources: Alissa Fock and Hans-Stefan Siller. (2025). Generative artificial intelligence in secondary STEM education in the light of Human Flourishing: a scoping literature review. International Journal of STEM Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40594-025-00589-5

article_title: From Design to Implementation to Practice a Learning by Teaching System: Betty’s Brain
citation: Gautam Biswas, James R. Segedy, Kritya Bunchongchit. (2016). From Design to Implementation to Practice: a Learning by Teaching System: Betty's Brain. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-015-0057-9
title: Hierarchical task model of open-ended learning environment tasks
description: The paper presents a hierarchical model characterizing the tasks students must perform to succeed in open-ended learning environments such as Betty's Brain, organized as "three broad classes of OELE tasks related to: (i) information seeking and acquisition, (ii) solution construction and refinement, and (iii) solution assessment." Each category is broken into three levels: general task descriptions common across OELEs, Betty's Brain specific instantiations, and system interface features. Directed links represent dependency relations, e.g., solution assessment depends on interpreting quiz results as actionable information for refining the solution in progress.
requirements: Students must learn to perform a diverse set of tasks across the model's three task classes to succeed in teaching Betty
constraints: The model was developed for OELEs generally and Betty's Brain more specifically
target_learning_goals: building and refining causal models of science phenomena
self-directed problem solving in open-ended tasks
examples: Used to explain why some students struggled: some are good readers unfamiliar with the causal modeling language; others fail to use quiz results to find correct and incorrect links.
key_sources: Gautam Biswas, James R. Segedy, Kritya Bunchongchit. (2016). From Design to Implementation to Practice: a Learning by Teaching System: Betty's Brain. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-015-0057-9

article_title: Optimizing practice scheduling requires quantitative tracking of individual item performance
citation: Luke G. Eglington and Philip I. Pavlik Jr. (2020). Optimizing practice scheduling requires quantitative tracking of individual item performance. npj Science of Learning 5:15. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-020-00074-4
title: Optimal Efficiency Threshold (OET) framework: model-based adaptive practice scheduling guided by microeconomic efficiency
description: The OET framework treats practice scheduling as an economic problem: choose for practice the item whose predicted recall probability is closest to (but below) a threshold that maximizes learning gains per unit of time. Efficiency is defined as "the gain in retrievability at some ﬁnal test divided by the time cost of the current practice", with utility weighting correct and incorrect trial gains and costs by the probability of correctness. A computational memory model tracks each item's practice history to estimate recall probability and RT. The framework was instantiated in simulations and a vocabulary-learning experiment.
requirements: An accurate computational model of recall probability fit to prior data with variety in spacings and repetitions
Tracking of individual item practice history and predicted recall probability during learning
constraints: The exact OET value varies across learning materials and feedback types; lower OETs may be preferable when failures provide larger or faster learning gains
Tested with word-pair learning as a simplifying assumption; complete models would need to account for inter-item relations and transfer
target_learners: students learning vocabulary or independent facts in online educational systems
examples: Simulations of 6 conventional and 22 model-scheduled conditions; an experiment comparing OETs 0.40–0.98 against a nonadaptive S15 control
key_sources: Luke G. Eglington and Philip I. Pavlik Jr. (2020). Optimizing practice scheduling requires quantitative tracking of individual item performance. npj Science of Learning 5:15. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-020-00074-4

article_title: International perspectives on using OER for online learning
citation: Lee, D., Lee, E. (2021). International perspectives on using OER for online learning. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-020-09871-5
title: OER-enabled pedagogy as a concept for future OER work
description: The article's reference list includes Wiley and Hilton's (2018) work "Defining OER-enabled pedagogy," indicating the commentary draws on this concept when suggesting future directions for OER use in online learning. The article itself offers no definition or elaboration of the concept beyond citing it, so it is recorded as a named framework the article points to without evidence or argument of its own.
requirements: The concept originates in Wiley and Hilton (2018), cited in the article's reference list
constraints: The article provides no definition, evidence, or argument for the concept beyond the citation
target_learning_goals: pedagogical use of open educational resources
key_sources: Lee, D., Lee, E. (2021). International perspectives on using OER for online learning. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-020-09871-5

article_title: Implementing open educational resources in digital education
citation: Tang, H. (2021). Implementing open educational resources in digital education. Education Tech Research Dev 69, 389–392. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-020-09879-x
title: Implementing OER in digital education requires considerations beyond OER efficacy
description: The article argues that adopting OER is not only a matter of demonstrated learning effectiveness: "implementing OER in digital education needs additional considerations beyond the efficacy of OER." It therefore recommends attending to research, design, culture, and practice perspectives when bringing OER into digital education, especially during rapid transitions to online teaching.
requirements: Educators and designers implementing OER should consider factors beyond efficacy, per the article's four-perspective framing
constraints: The article does not specify in the provided text which additional considerations apply under which conditions
target_learners: online learners during emergency remote teaching
target_learning_goals: sustaining teaching and learning through digital education with OER
examples: The editorial motivates this principle with the COVID-19-driven demand for online educational resources and the rapid transition to digital education
key_sources: Tang, H. (2021). Implementing open educational resources in digital education. Education Tech Research Dev 69, 389–392. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-020-09879-x

article_title: Implementing open educational resources in digital education
citation: Tang, H. (2021). Implementing open educational resources in digital education. Education Tech Research Dev 69, 389–392. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-020-09879-x
title: Open educational resources (OER) as cost-saving, openly licensed resources for digital education
description: Open educational resources (OER) are educational materials with "the benefits of cost-saving and open licenses." The article presents OER as having "great potential in facilitating the rapid transition to digital education," particularly in response to the increased demand for online educational resources during the COVID-19 outbreak. Their effectiveness for student learning is the subject of ongoing scrutiny in the article.
requirements: Open licenses and cost savings are the defining benefits the article attributes to OER
constraints: Concerns about whether OER decrease the effectiveness of student learning remain unsolved, per the article
target_learning_goals: access to affordable learning materials in digital education
examples: The article cites OER use in college textbook adoption and K-12 teacher practice through its reference list
key_sources: Tang, H. (2021). Implementing open educational resources in digital education. Education Tech Research Dev 69, 389–392. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-020-09879-x

article_title: The Motivation Impact of Open Educational Resources Utilization on Physics Learning Using Quipper School App
citation: Sulisworo, D., Sulistiyo, E. N., & Akhsan, R. N. (2017). The motivation impact of open educational resources utilization on physics learning using Quipper School app. Turkish Online Journal of Distance Education-TOJDE, 18(4), Article 9. https://tojde.anadolu.edu.tr
title: Blended physics learning pattern splitting discussion to class time and reading, tasks and exercises to the OER platform
description: The article's learning activities pattern runs a full semester following the school's lesson plans for class XI physics. Face-to-face class sessions are reserved for discussion of material, tasks and exercises, while reading, tasks and exercises are done online through Quipper School, with teacher-student chat and message interaction for certain things. The article states "The more materials on the LMS make it easier for teachers to choose materials and activities appropriate to the characteristics of classroom management."
requirements: Availability of varied learning materials on the LMS so teachers can select activities fitting classroom management
constraints: Implemented in this study for one semester of grade XI physics in an Indonesian high school
target_learners: high school grade XI physics students
target_learning_goals: physics content learning with sustained motivation
examples: The treatment group learned via this blended pattern for one semester and scored higher on attention, relevance, and confidence than the face-to-face control group.
key_sources: Sulisworo, D., Sulistiyo, E. N., & Akhsan, R. N. (2017). The motivation impact of open educational resources utilization on physics learning using Quipper School app. Turkish Online Journal of Distance Education-TOJDE, 18(4), Article 9. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1161803
